hints: Look carefully at the Venn diagram. Letter A is right in the middle, so ask yourself what feature is shared by chloroplasts, mitochondria AND nuclei.
Remember which of these three structures contain their own DNA that needs to be copied before division.
walkthrough:
**Spot what the question is really asking**

Think simply: semi-conservative replication only happens where DNA is found. So we need to find the region that includes every structure that contains DNA.

**Recall which structures have DNA**

Nuclei have linear DNA. Both mitochondria and chloroplasts have small circular DNA, a clue to their prokaryotic origin. All three therefore replicate their DNA semi-conservatively.

**Read the Venn diagram**

Letter A is the overlap of all three circles: chloroplasts, mitochondria and nuclei. That is the only letter that correctly includes every site of DNA replication.

options.A: Correct. A is common to chloroplasts, mitochondria and nuclei, and all three contain DNA that replicates semi-conservatively.
options.B: Incorrect. B is only the overlap of chloroplasts and nuclei, so it wrongly leaves out mitochondria which also have DNA.
options.C: Incorrect. C is nuclei only, so it wrongly leaves out the DNA found in both mitochondria and chloroplasts.
options.D: Incorrect. D is only the overlap of mitochondria and nuclei, so it wrongly leaves out chloroplasts which also have DNA.
